overall: Violation found: a hybrid meeting largely inaudible to remote attendees was not truly open. No ADA accommodation violation; public-comment and muting allegations declined as chair's discretion.

allegations.summary: The July 16 hybrid meeting was largely inaudible to remote attendees for extended periods, so remote access was not real-time.
allegations.key_passage: For those who attended remotely and could not follow the Committee’s deliberations, the meeting was not truly open to the public.

allegations.summary: Remote attendees were denied the same access as in-person attendees, including chat and camera use, limiting their ability to communicate and comment.
allegations.key_passage: Public participation in a remote or hybrid meeting is left to the discretion of the chair, just as it is with a meeting conducted in person.

allegations.summary: A remote attendee's microphone was muted arbitrarily during the meeting, effectively cutting off her public comment.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law permits the chair of a public body to decide who may speak at a meeting and for how long.

allegations.summary: The committee allegedly failed to provide reasonable accommodation and effective access, based on the denied chat and camera request.
allegations.key_passage: Because there was no request for a reasonable accommodation of a disability, the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
